title: Measurement of the Degree of Deacetylation in Chitosan Films by FTIR, 1H NMR and UV Spectrophotometry
author: Sánchez-Machado, López-Cervantes, et al.
materials: Chitosan was obtained from different sources and deacetylation methods. The conventional deacetylation method was a thermoalkaline hydrolysis with 45% NaOH at 110°C for 2 hours with constant stirring. Additionally, the microwave deacetylation method was performed with 45% NaOH at 200 W for 23 min. With both methods, the kinetic reactions were performed until the deacetylation of chitosan was reached.

steps.title: Conventional thermoalkaline deacetylation
steps.instruction: Perform conventional deacetylation by heating chitosan in 45 % NaOH solution at 110 °C for 2 h with constant stirring, continuing until deacetylation is reached.

steps.title: Microwave‑assisted deacetylation
steps.instruction: Perform microwave deacetylation by treating chitosan in 45 % NaOH solution at 200 W for 23 min, continuing until deacetylation is reached.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare two stock solutions in 0.1 N HCl: D‑glucosamine (7.49 mM, Cg) and N‑acetylglucosamine (0.49 mM, Ca). Mix these stocks in varying proportions to generate 12 working solutions covering N‑acetylglucosamine concentrations 0.06–0.24 mM and D‑glucosamine concentrations 0.12–6 mM for the calibration curve.

steps.title: Measure calibration absorbance
steps.instruction: Record the absorbance of each of the 12 calibration solutions at 201 nm using a UV‑VIS Genesys 10 spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Prepare film sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 2 mg of chitosan film, dissolve in 0.1 N HCl and dilute to a final volume of 10 mL.

steps.title: Measure sample absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of the dissolved film solution at 201 nm with the same UV‑VIS Genesys 10 instrument.

steps.title: Calculate degree of deacetylation
steps.instruction: Determine the calibration line slope (k) and intercept (c) from the calibration curve. Then compute DA using DA = ((179.1 × A × V) – (c × m))/((k × m) – (42.1 × A × V)), where A is the sample absorbance, V is the total volume in liters (0.010 L), and m is the sample mass in mg (2 mg). Finally calculate %DD = (1 – DA) × 100.

substeps.instruction: Determine calibration line slope (k) and intercept (c) from the calibration curve.
Calculate DA using the provided equation.
